Edit the 3D by hand

Drag the corners of the faceted sculpture to correct it: a muzzle, an ear, a foot.

Drag a corner
moves it; with Shift, straight in or out of the surface
Drop it on a corner next to it
the two become one (one face less)
Drag the middle of a face
moves the whole face
Shift + click on corners
picks several: dragging one moves them all
Alt + click on a face
adds a corner there
Ctrl + click on a corner (⌘ on the Mac)
removes it (also Delete with the pointer on it)
Shift + Alt + click near a side
turns the diagonal between its two faces
Ctrl + Shift + click on a face
puts the faces around it on one plane

The edits stay in the project and come back when the sculpture is recalculated with the same faces.

Detail brush

Each click adds an area: "more detail" keeps faces (muzzle, paws), "less detail" removes them (back, flanks). The total number of faces stays as set.

Sheet and cutting
°

0° = every face is a separate piece. Higher = larger sections to bend and fewer welds.

Hand bending

Quick assembly

Three small strips with teeth, notches with five different plays and bend lines with three bridges: cut them on your sheet, try them, then write the best play above.

Base plate

Structure and stability

Flat frames across the sculpture, welded inside the shell: they keep large sculptures from flexing. Each rib is engraved with its number and distance from the end.

Laser output

Every DXF of the program (sculptures, metalwork, 2D drawing) leaves with these settings. Try the first file on the machine before cutting a whole job.

2D parts

Flat parts drawn to measure that go with the work (brackets, fixing plates, a plaque): same material, their own thickness (empty = that of the work), nested by thickness, with their engravings and texts in the DXF, and in the quote.
